questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why Norway has the best health system
How to stop feeling unhappy at work
How ideas about happiness differ between cultures
Why older people are happier than young people
questions.why: Neil says they are talking about concepts of happiness, which vary from culture to culture.

questions.q: Which of these does Rob say makes him happy?
options: Being healthy and having good friends
Travelling to New Zealand and spending time outdoors
Earning a lot of money
Spending time alone
questions.why: Rob mentions being healthy, having good friends and presenting the programme with Neil.

questions.q: According to research, how do East Asian cultures tend to see happiness?
options: As personal feelings of pleasure
As shared experiences and family
As having a successful career
As social harmony
questions.why: The research says East Asian cultures tend to see happiness as social harmony.

questions.q: Which country did Helen Russell find to be one of the happiest?
options: New Zealand
Japan
England
India
questions.why: Neil says 'Actually no. It was Japan.' after Rob guesses New Zealand.

questions.q: What is the idea behind the Japanese concept of wabi-sabi?
options: Hiding signs of age for as long as you possibly can
Throwing away things that are broken
Seeing beauty in things that are not perfect
Working hard to make everything perfect
questions.why: Helen Russell describes it as 'celebrating imperfection' and seeing beauty in ageing.

questions.q: Why does Helen Russell mention kintsugi, mending broken pots with gold?
options: To show damage can be highlighted, not hidden
To explain why traditional Japanese pottery is so expensive
To suggest a new hobby for unhappy people
To compare Japanese and British art
questions.why: She says the scars, rather than being hidden, are 'highlighted in pure gold', like celebrating our laughter lines.

questions.q: What does Helen Russell say about English people?
options: They are the happiest people in Europe
They complain more than any other nation
They have no way of dealing with problems
They are 'jolly' and just get on with things
questions.why: She says the English have 'jolly', a coping mechanism where you just get on with things.

questions.q: What does Helen Russell think about this English 'jolly' attitude?
options: It is only found in upper-class people
It isn't perfect, but it has worked for many Brits
It is the main reason why English people are so happy
It is disappearing because of modern comedy
questions.why: She says 'it's not perfect but it's worked for many Brits for a while'.
